venue_assessment.waterfront_breakwater: Italian pasta, $$, four meat-free mains, no cheese/butter/cream, never any peanuts, nothing fried. Meets everything: 3 stars.
venue_assessment.waterfront_tidewater: Greek, misses the pasta craving; otherwise safe (no peanuts, dairy-free, vegetarian mains, light, $$). 2 stars. Decoy built on Roxy's 'greek place' line.
venue_assessment.waterfront_keel_street: Peanuts in the pesto, caponata and salad. Deal-breaker.
venue_assessment.waterfront_marina_arch: No main without meat or fish. Deal-breaker for Mina.
venue_assessment.waterfront_pier_nine: Dairy everywhere. Intolerance costs a star: 2 stars.
venue_assessment.waterfront_bluewater: Everything fried, heavy. Misses Brooke's preference: 2 stars.

notes: Solvable and fair: every decoy fails on exactly one constraint, and Breakwater's reviews clear each one explicitly.

The pasta craving comes in as a counter to Roxy's Greek suggestion rather than a direct ask. That's a nice touch, but a player who skims could read Roxy's line as the craving and pick Tidewater (2 stars).
Marina Arch's first review sounds great ('all olive oil and lemon'), and only the second review shows it has no meat-free mains. That's a good trap and it's fair.
Mina's line ('a few dishes to choose from') is a soft way to state a strict diet. I treated it as vegetarian, a deal-breaker. That works for Marina Arch either way, since it has zero meat-free mains.
Liam's 'fried fish off a pier' line hints that fried food is off, and so does Brooke's 'not one more heavy thing'. Together they point clearly at Bluewater as the wrong pick.
